The passage employs personification to transform the classroom clock into a "stern schoolmaster," symbolizing the rigid, authoritative control that institutional structures exert over students. By describing the ticking hands as having an "unyielding authority" and holding students in a "temporal grip," the text uses metaphor to illustrate how time is not just a neutral measure but an active, oppressive force that dictates the rhythm of academic life, stripping students of autonomy.

Regarding your priority question: The animal typically regarded as man's best friend is the dog.
